walkthroughs.body_html:
V = IR.

Ohmic: R constant. Most resistors.
Non-ohmic: filament (R rises with T), diode (one-way).

I = ΔQ/Δt. If 12 V battery drives 0.5 A through R, then R = 24 Ω.

Series: R_total = R₁ + R₂ +. Current same; voltages share.

Parallel: 1/R_total = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ +. Voltage same; currents share.

Two equal R in parallel = R/2.
Two equal R in series = 2R.

1st (current): ΣI_in = ΣI_out at each junction (charge conservation).

2nd (voltage): ΣV = 0 around any loop (energy conservation).

Power: P = IV = I²R = V²/R.

Domestic 1500 W kettle on 230 V: I = 6.5 A.

mcqs.q: In which direction does an electric field point near a positive charge?
options: Radially outwards — the field is defined by the force on a positive test charge, which is repelled.
There is no field around a positive charge unless another charge is present.
Radially inwards because positive attracts negative.

mcqs.q: What does the cosmological redshift of distant galaxies indicate?
options: Only when the force is small enough to be ignored.
Space itself is expanding, stretching the wavelength of light from distant galaxies as it travels.
Galaxies are moving through space away from us, like objects flying outward from a centre.
